singlePointsOfFailure.risk: The layered authorization engine is the single enforcement point consumed by every server function (AGENTS 27). An outage or defect in authorization.ts silently widens the system unless it fails closed. It is also the least directly tested universal module (STREAM H: no dedicated authorization.test.ts).
singlePointsOfFailure.mitigation: Fail-closed default decision; exhaustive dedicated suite (L-H-022); decision log auditability (V1CAP-016 contract).

singlePointsOfFailure.risk: Universal kernel reality substrate (cg_entity/cg_relationship/cg_event/cg_observation) underpins every fabric; 20260903000000 migration is AUTHORED-NOT-APPLIED to canonical environments.
Identity substrate: every actor resolution flows through it; revocation failure would invalidate all downstream authorization.
singlePointsOfFailure.mitigation: Revocation proofs owed under V1CAP-020 (J-009); revocation fail-closed invariant is a mandatory test battery.

singlePointsOfFailure.risk: Mission orchestration spine has a single (ratification-pending) owner — CG-GAP-003/COND-001. Owner ambiguity is itself an availability SPOF for the loop.
singlePointsOfFailure.mitigation: Ratification is an owned blocking gap with deliverable kind 'artifact'.

singlePointsOfFailure.risk: The phase-01 verify pipeline is the only verification authority for nearly all V1 claims — a verification-infrastructure SPOF. Its green baseline (3,458 tests) is reproducible in a bare VM (STREAM H evidence).

dependency.verdict: HEALTHY GRAPH, CONTAMINATED EDGES. The 93-capability V1 dependency graph is acyclic and the critical path is well-ordered (authorization primitives first, environment truth second, mission/worker spine third, evidence tail last). Single points of failure are concentrated at V1CAP-016/001/010 and are mitigable with fail-closed design plus the owed test batteries. The structural defect is not topology but vocabulary: six layering violations put Scholar domain vocabulary inside universal/kernel/control-plane layers (I-018/I-019/I-025/I-027 plus STREAM H relocation debt) — these are tracked as hardening requirements L-H-023 and do not reorder the critical path.

threat.threat: Scholar-fused universal authorization primitives: every universal cg_ substrate RPC (cg_role_assignment, cg_org_profile, workforce positions) is gated on is_school_admin()/get_my_school_id() resolved from public.users.school_id (migrations 20260907000300..00800; I-001..I-005). A non-Scholar tenant can neither hold nor administer any role assignment; conversely the platform's authorization truth is anchored to a domain slice table, so tenant authorization resolution is structurally wrong for every future runtime.
threat.existingMitigation: Deny-by-default RLS with zero policies on cg_org_unit/cg_org_membership (20261001000000, applied to dev with RLS check PASS); the migrations deliberately refuse to wire Scholar helpers into the universal model (I-007 evidence).
threat.requiredMitigation: Neutral tenant-membership DB primitives (get_my_tenant_id() + holds_tenant_role(p_tenant, p_role_ref)) resolved from cg_role_assignment/cg_org_membership; re-gate every universal-substrate RPC on them; demote users.school_id semantics behind the Scholar adapter (J-005, blocked on COND-003 tenant_id type ruling). Hardened by L-H-001.

threat.threat: Cross-tenant information disclosure via unproven RLS: the 'RLS enabled with zero policies = deny' posture on every cg_ table is statically reasoned, not database-proven in CI (STREAM H unverifiedImplementations). A single malformed future policy grants Tenant A access to Tenant B — the mandatory AGENTS 31 invariant — with no CI gate to catch it.
threat.existingMitigation: Tenant resolution is server-side (tenant spoofing impossible via API governance); cross-tenant rejection live-tested once on the dev project; scripts/run-rls-isolation-check.mjs exists but requires live credentials; the two applied V1 migrations passed an RLS isolation check at application time.
threat.requiredMitigation: RLS isolation battery executed with live credentials in CI on every merge (V1CAP-073/J-041, hardened by L-H-008); battery failure blocks merge; battery covers Tenant-A-cannot-see-Tenant-B, revoked-fails, expired-fails per AGENTS 31.

threat.threat: Delegation privilege escalation: a worker (AI or human) receives a delegation and performs actions beyond the principal's authority, or re-delegates to expand its own reach. Mission/Delegation object contracts are unowned and unwritten (J-024/J-025) and persistent governed worker definitions with authority bounds do not exist (J-027, LAUNCH_BLOCKER).
threat.existingMitigation: frontend/src/lib/control-plane/foundation-loop.ts is a pure plan engine — the caller cannot supply tenant or verification decision; agent-runtime/mission-runner.ts PLANS ONLY (execution stays with the foundation loop); authorization.ts Invariant 12: no autonomous agent may silently escalate its own authority.
threat.requiredMitigation: First-class bounded, revocable, non-escalating delegation contracts with acting-on-behalf-of semantics (J-025); persistent worker definitions whose capability set is identity-linked and authority-bounded (J-027); every delegated action re-resolves through V1CAP-016 under the principal's constraints. Hardened by L-H-004/L-H-005.

threat.threat: Self-verification: a worker verifies its own output inside the loop, converting generated claims into 'verified' status without independent judgment. Verification independence is required by the corpus (E-050: an AI worker must not validate its own unsupported claim) but is not enforced anywhere (J-035).
threat.existingMitigation: The live-verified foundation loop structurally separates admission from verification (frontend/src/lib/control-plane/foundation-mission.ts pure admit/verify engine; foundation-loop.ts refuses caller-supplied verification decisions; cg_verification_result is a distinct table in 20260929000000).
threat.requiredMitigation: Verification independence enforcement generalized across the loop: verifier identity must differ from producer identity for every verification result; violations recorded as nonconformance (J-035). Hardened by L-H-009.

threat.threat: Prompt injection through untrusted context: attacker-controlled content (customer messages, external documents, agent-retrieved artifacts) smuggles instructions into AI context and redirects model behavior into unauthorized actions. AI-specific runtime defenses (injection defense, exfiltration control, malicious-artifact defense) are declared but not implemented (J-036).
threat.existingMitigation: frontend/src/lib/context-assembly.ts: UNTRUSTED wrapping of externally-derived content with enforced downstream delimitation; the assembler never re-classifies untrusted content into trusted instructions, never grants authority, and every dropped candidate is audited with an explicit reason; gateway-centralization is mechanically enforced (tests/unit/ai-gateway-adoption-*.test.ts).
threat.requiredMitigation: Implement J-036 defenses at the gateway/runtime layer (V1CAP-033): injection-resistant prompt delimitation enforcement, exfiltration controls on outputs, malicious-artifact scanning for worker-ingested files, supply-chain checks on tool/model integrations. Hardened by L-H-014.

threat.threat: Evidence-class laundering: AI-generated, simulated or predicted content silently enters the record as direct observation, so downstream verification and canonical truth rest on fabricated provenance (J-034; Constitution §9 canonical-truth principle).
threat.existingMitigation: Evidence-class capture discipline is a named V1 capability on the critical path (V1CAP-059, impl=false); context-assembly trust classification (classifyContextTrust in ai-context.ts) marks source kinds at assembly time; cg_foundation_evidence records carry class fields in 20260929000000.
threat.requiredMitigation: Capture-time class enforcement: generated/simulated/predicted evidence can never silently become direct observation — the class is set at capture, immutable in the evidence store, and any promotion path requires an explicit governed verification step (L-H-010).

threat.threat: Gateway bypass: a caller invokes a model provider directly (or through a fallback path) escaping authorization, budget pre-check, rate limiting and metering — unmetered, unlogged, unauthorized AI spend and data flow.
threat.existingMitigation: Gateway centralization is mechanically test-enforced today: no @ai-sdk/createOpenAICompatible import exists outside ai-gateway* (tests/unit/ai-gateway-adoption-expense-insights/lesson-plan/timetable.test.ts); ai-gateway.server.ts fail-closed invariants (BLK-2 missing key → explicit unconfigured decision, never a live attempt); budget pre-check and rate limiting inside invokeAiGateway.
threat.requiredMitigation: Defense beyond import-lint: runtime egress enforcement (network policy allowing provider calls only from the gateway), model registry rejecting unregistered models, and fallback models inheriting the identical policy gates (J-014). Hardened by L-H-018.

threat.threat: Secret exfiltration through logs, context payloads, or the AI gateway: credential material (AI_API_KEY, deploy credentials, payment keys) leaks into structured logs, model prompts, or worker memory — creating a reusable exfiltration channel to external providers.
threat.existingMitigation: ai-gateway.server.ts: no key material ever reaches a log line; every emitted field is scrubbed against the live key as defense in depth; observability/structured-log.ts is a secret-redacting JSON-line logger; scripts/verification/secret-scan.mjs runs in npm run verify (PASS baseline); BLK secret family provisioned only via Cursor Dashboard (RULING-11/COND-006), never in repo.
threat.requiredMitigation: Per-agent credential broker with no universal master credential, secret isolation, rotation and blast-radius containment per credential (J-007); context assembly structurally excludes credential-class material from AI payloads. Hardened by L-H-015.

threat.threat: Payment webhook forgery or replay: an attacker posts a forged or replayed webhook to convert it into a financial effect (credit, entitlement, settlement) without a real charge. Live signature verification has never been exercised (BLK-4) and idempotency exists only on the foundation loop, not as a cross-module standard (J-030).
threat.existingMitigation: frontend/src/lib/payments/replay-guard.ts: two rejection axes (seen event ids = duplicates; event timestamps outside 300s tolerance = stale/future replay indicators), stateless-in/stateless-out and unit-tested (tests/unit/payments-replay-guard.test.ts); adapters signature-validated against recorded semantics; webhook-source-of-truth posture stated in AGENTS 36.
threat.requiredMitigation: Live signature-verified webhook evidence under BLK-4 (COND-006) before any live rail; universal mandatory idempotency keys on all consequential commands (J-030); webhook processing behind the governed server-function chain (authenticate → resolve tenant → authorize → validate → execute → audit). Hardened by L-H-020/L-H-017.

threat.threat: Cross-tenant event/realtime broadcast: an event, subscription or notification delivers another tenant's state change to a subscriber — the realtime plane leaks what the RLS plane denies (AGENTS 35: never broadcast unauthorized events). Per-event security contract and tenant-scoped routing are unbuilt (J-021/J-022).
threat.existingMitigation: V1CAP-012 security boundary states realtime broadcasts are tenant-filtered; harden-schools-and-realtime migration (20260819000000) established tenant-scoped realtime precedent on Scholar slice tables; per-event security contract is a named V1 capability (V1CAP-044, impl=false).
threat.requiredMitigation: Per-event security contract on every event (authenticity, authorization, privacy, provenance carried per-event, J-022); tenant-scoped subscription delivery with replay and backpressure (J-021); delivery authorization evaluated per-subscriber, not per-channel. Hardened by L-H-011/L-H-025.

threat.threat: File-plane path escape: a crafted contentRef/storage path escapes the tenant path prefix in storage-adapter.server.ts, reading or writing another tenant's object. The V1 file plane has no substrate migration — the adapter's path-convention prefix is the only tenant enforcement below the pure access policy.
threat.existingMitigation: frontend/src/lib/files/access-policy.ts: deny-by-default with explicit reasons; cross-tenant access ALWAYS denied including for platform super-admins (no control-plane bypass in V1); grants honored only while unexpired; RLS remains the declared boundary and the adapter independently enforces the tenant path prefix; unit suites exist (tests/unit/files-*.test.ts).
threat.requiredMitigation: Adversarial path tests (traversal, encoding, prefix-confusion) added to the storage-adapter suite; a V1 file substrate table with tenant-scoped RLS so the database — not only a path convention — carries the boundary; grants bound to V1CAP-016 decisions.

threat.threat: Command replay outside the foundation loop: consequential commands (workflow transitions, payment operations, notifications, worker tasks) are retried or maliciously re-submitted, double-executing financial or state effects because idempotency keys are not a cross-module standard (J-030).
threat.existingMitigation: Foundation loop idempotent replay is live-verified (second call returned replayed=true with the same executionId on the dev project, tests/integration/foundation-loop.live.test.ts); workflow engine (workflow-engine.ts) is a pure evaluator where UNKNOWN is never TRUE; payments carry the replay guard.
threat.requiredMitigation: Mandatory idempotency keys on every consequential command across all modules (J-030), enforced at the execution-system layer (V1CAP-053/054) with duplicate submissions returning the original result, never re-executing. Hardened by L-H-017.

threat.threat: Escalation and approval abuse: the ESCALATE and REQUIRE_APPROVAL decision outcomes have no wired approval chains (J-032) and no emergency lockdown path (J-010), so an escalation either dead-ends (DoS on legitimate operations) or is resolved by an ungoverned shortcut; guardians themselves could become an unmonitored privilege path.
threat.existingMitigation: frontend/src/lib/authorization.ts implements the five-valued decision model (ALLOW|DENY|REDACT|ESCALATE|REQUIRE_APPROVAL) with Invariant 12 (no silent agent self-escalation); jarvis-contract.ts encodes the Part 15 executive-orchestrator boundary where every MUST-NOT is an enforced deny (tests/unit/jarvis-contract.test.ts); workflow-engine.ts requires a human approval record for approval steps.
threat.requiredMitigation: Risk-classified approval routing through the one canonical workflow lifecycle (J-032): approval chains wired to high-risk actions with human approval records; emergency revocation/lockdown with security guardians who are themselves governed identities (J-010); every ESCALATE outcome resolves through an owned, audited flow. Hardened by L-H-016.

threat.threat: Environment-state falsification: claims of 'live-verified' resting on a database whose canonical posture is 'AUTHORED, NOT APPLIED' let insecure or drifted schema be treated as deployed truth. The dev/canonical evidence-class split (STREAM H contradiction) is exactly the surface where unapplied security posture gets reported as proven.
threat.existingMitigation: The two approved V1 migrations (20260930000000 workspace persistence, 20261001000000 org model) were applied to the dev project via the authorized management-API path with an RLS isolation check PASS and rowsecurity=true verified on all four tables (COREGRID_CTO_DIRECTIVE_RECONCILIATION.json disposition); drift between declared and applied schema is already designated a blocking nonconformance in the V1CAP-072 security boundary.
threat.requiredMitigation: Applied-migration manifest as environment state truth (J-040): every canonical environment records exactly which migrations are applied; cg_* substrate applied to canonical environments; reporting may never conflate 'live-verified once on dev' with 'deployed' (scope-lock unresolved item honored). Hardened by L-H-003.

threat.threat: Memory retrieval authorization bypass: persisted memory retrieval (especially vector/similarity search) returns records the querier could not have read directly, bypassing tenant, role and scope filters — 'memory must not be a side door around authorization' (J-017); worker memory scopes can silently expand (J-018/J-029).
threat.existingMitigation: Memory retrieval is a named V1 capability (V1CAP-036, impl=false) whose security boundary requires authorization-gated, non-vector-only retrieval; memory governance boundary (V1CAP-037) reserves ownership with the platform, not the agent; the persisted memory store itself does not exist yet (J-016, COND-002 gated).
threat.requiredMitigation: Every retrieval result filtered by identity AND tenant AND scope AND policy before return (post-filter AND pre-query scope constraints, not vector-similarity-only); worker memory scopes (session/mission/long-term) enforced with no silent expansion (J-029). Hardened by L-H-019.

threat.threat: Context-switch bleed: one user operating across multiple realities/tenants retains prior-scope tokens, cached context packages or workspace state after switching, so post-switch requests are served under stale authorization context (J-012).
threat.existingMitigation: V1CAP-024 is a named capability with a fail-closed security boundary ('post-switch requests must fail closed if any prior-scope token persists'); context packages are ephemeral-plus-trace-persisted by design in context-assembly.ts; workspace state is projection-layer, not canonical.
threat.requiredMitigation: Context-switch safety implementation: on switch, all prior-scope tokens and assembled context packages are invalidated; post-switch requests fail closed if any prior-scope token persists; switch events audited (L-H-021).

failure.recovery: Automatic: none required — the gateway refuses rather than degrades. Recovery is operator action (provision BLK-2 key). Fallback/failover and circuit breaker do not exist yet (J-014).
failure.blastRadius: All AI features (V1CAP-027 inference, lesson-plan/expense insights adoption paths). No security impact — failure is fail-closed.
failure.verdict: adequate at contract level; gap for live-path failure semantics (no circuit breaker, no fallback — J-014/L-H-018)

failure.detection: Live battery probes + scripts/probe-foundation-database.mjs; structured logs; evidence tail absence is visible.

failure.blastRadius: Single mission; no partial state corruption (append-only cg_execution_history).

failure.recovery: State machine parks in honest non-delivered states; no retry/backoff policy authored.
failure.blastRadius: Communication fabric stalls honestly; no false-positive delivery evidence.

failure.detection: Pure, attribution-complete ledger with unit suite; budget decisions typed (BudgetDecision).
failure.recovery: Gateway budget pre-check fails closed if the ledger is unreadable — cost failure cannot produce unmetered spend.
failure.blastRadius: AI operations pause (fail-closed), which is the correct direction.
failure.verdict: adequate; cost rollup to tenant/mission is open (J-043)

assumptions: Target order of magnitude: tens of thousands of entities (people, devices, buildings, twins) per tenant and thousands of tenants — the reconstruction's loop model (per-tenant reality substrate over cg_* tables) must hold at this scale without per-entity resident processes.
AI volume is bounded by the gateway: every inference is metered, budget pre-checked and rate-limited inside invokeAiGateway (ai-gateway.server.ts); there is no unmetered AI path.
Worker execution is delegation-driven: workers are ephemeral runtimes executing bounded delegations from the foundation loop, not long-lived daemons per entity.
Event volume grows with entity activity; the outbox (kernel/outbox.ts) is the single emission point feeding the evidence fabric (V1CAP-041→V1CAP-057 integration point).
limits: No resource quotas or lease/concurrency control exist (J-031): concurrent workers over shared resources can thrash; mission throughput is unbounded above by anything except gateway rate limits.
Event routing/subscriptions lack backpressure (J-021): fan-out amplification is possible as tenant count grows.
No persisted memory store (J-016) and no retrieval index design: memory-dependent loop iteration is unbounded per request today (in-memory only).
Single-process rate limiting in the gateway: multi-instance deployment (V1CAP-076 path) requires distributed rate-limit state — currently in-process.

Registry-driven capability resolution (V1CAP-082) and 3,458-test verify pipeline: CI cost grows linearly with phases; test attribution debt (1,230 unattributed tests) makes scale-level regression triage slow (J-046).
scalability.ephemeralAgentCompliance: COMPLIANT AS DESIGNED, PROVISIONAL IN EVIDENCE. The runtime model is ephemeral-by-mission: frontend/src/lib/agent-runtime/ephemeral-lifecycle.ts governs agent instantiation, and agent-runtime/mission-runner.ts plans only — execution stays with the governed foundation loop, so there is no resident agent per entity. Agents are first-class identities whose durable parts are data (identity rows, capability registry entries, delegation records, memory scopes), not processes: 50k entities therefore mean 50k governable identity/capability records plus a bounded pool of ephemeral worker runtimes, satisfying the 'no 50k resident agents' requirement. The provisional part: persistent governed worker definitions with authority bounds do not exist yet (J-027/L-H-005), so today compliance rests on the plans-only mission runner rather than on enforced durable definitions. Once L-H-005 lands, the data-not-process model is structural, not conventional.
scalability.verdict: ADEQUATE FOR V1-SCALE IF QUOTAS LAND. The loop's security-relevant scaling property (ephemeral agents, metered gateway, append-only evidence) is architecturally sound; the scaling gaps are operational (quotas/leases J-031, event backpressure J-021, distributed rate limiting) rather than architectural. None of these blocks first loop closure; all are required before multi-tenant production load.

metered: AI inference: every call through ai-gateway.server.ts is cost-estimated (estimateCostUsd), budget pre-checked (evaluateBudget → typed BudgetDecision), rate-limited and metered into metering/usage-ledger.ts — attribution-complete and pure; bypass is architecturally prevented and test-enforced.
Gateway purposes are constrained to organizational intelligence by the metering vocabulary (no ad-hoc purposes).
unmeteredExposure: Model fallback/failover (J-014 absent): a fallback provider would need identical metering; until the model registry exists, fallback semantics are undefined and would be an unmetered surface if ad-hoc.
File storage and egress: no V1 file substrate table, no storage metering; storage growth is invisible to budgets.
Email/push/communication dispatch when BLK-5 lifts: dispatch-planner exists but provider cost attribution is not wired to the usage ledger.
Worker compute: no quotas/leases (J-031) — worker execution time is not attributed to mission or tenant.
Event fan-out compute (J-021): broadcast amplification cost is unattributed.
cost.budgetEnforcement: Enforced today only at the AI gateway: budget pre-check precedes invocation and exhaustion yields a typed refusal, not silent degradation (matches V1CAP-077's boundary 'budget exhaustion triggers review, not silent degradation'). Cost attribution to tenant/mission rollups does not exist (J-043) — spend is recorded but not attributable in reports. No budget mechanism exists for storage, messaging or worker compute.
cost.verdict: STRONG ON AI, ABSENT ELSEWHERE. The AI cost plane is the exemplar: metered, attributed, fail-closed. Every other V1 cost surface (storage, communication, worker compute, event fan-out) is unmetered exposure. Required: J-043 cost rollups and quota-backed budget enforcement beyond the gateway (covered by L-H-025 and the J-031 quotas requirement); not mission-launch-blocking.

tenancy.model: Shared-database multi-tenancy: every row carries tenant identity; access is enforced by PostgreSQL RLS (deny-by-default, zero policies until a neutral membership helper exists) plus server-resolved tenant context (tenant spoofing impossible via API governance — client tenant IDs never trusted, AGENTS 26). Tenant roots: cg_tenant (20260904020000, authored-not-applied) with legacy public.schools as the Scholar-slice tenant root (I-001/I-009).
enforcementLayers: Database: RLS on every cg_ table, deny-by-default; verified rowsecurity=true on the four applied dev tables (RLS check PASS)
Server functions: AGENTS 27 chain (authenticate → resolve tenant → authorize → validate → execute → audit); IdentityActor carries tenant scope (identity-actor.ts — currently schoolId-typed, I-011)
Authorization engine: V1CAP-016 five-valued decisions consumed by every server function (fan-in 19)
Capability gate: capability-gate.ts evaluates runtime-declared features (currently hard-coded 'r001', I-012)
File plane: storage-adapter tenant path prefix + deny-by-default access-policy (cross-tenant denied even for super-admins)
Realtime: tenant-filtered broadcasts per V1CAP-012 boundary (per-event contract unbuilt, J-022)
knownWeakPoints: I-001: public.users fuses universal identity with Scholar slice (school_id uuid NOT NULL, Scholar role CHECK) — the canonical identity store is a domain table
I-002: get_my_school_id()/is_school_admin()/get_my_role() used as universal authorization primitives
I-003: cg_role_assignment/cg_role_grant RPCs (universal substrate) gated on Scholar helpers — non-Scholar tenants cannot hold or administer roles
I-004: cg_org_profile (declared domain-neutral) gated on is_school_admin AND own tenant
I-005: workforce position RPCs default p_runtime to 'runtime:scholar' and gate on Scholar helpers
I-011/I-012: IdentityActor.schoolId + capability-gate MEMBERSHIP_FOR_NAV_KIND/'r001' hard-code Scholar vocabulary in the universal access path
J-041: RLS isolation is statically reasoned, not CI-proven
COND-003: tenant_id type divergence (text vs uuid, 20261001000000 lines 32-37) blocks finalizing the neutral helper (J-005)
tenancy.verdict: SOUND POSTURE, COMPROMISED PRIMITIVES. The tenancy model (RLS floor + server-resolved context + layered authorization) matches AGENTS 13/17/26 and the deny-by-default law. But the primitives the enforcement layers resolve from are Scholar-fused (I-001..I-005, I-011/I-012): today the platform cannot legitimately authorize a non-Scholar tenant at the database layer at all. This is the single most important tenancy hardening (L-H-001/L-H-002) and is already the top of the critical path (V1CAP-013→014). Verdict: gap pending L-H-001/L-H-002/L-H-008.

authorization.neutralModelRequirement: Consolidated from STREAM I (neutralRoleModelRequirement) and the K-ruling synthesis: (1) closed domain-neutral ROLE VOCABULARY — ACTOR, MEMBER, OWNER, ADMINISTRATOR, OPERATOR, MANAGER, SUPERVISOR, CONTRIBUTOR, REVIEWER, APPROVER, AUDITOR, WORKER, AGENT, SERVICE, SYSTEM — owned by the platform (P02/P08), never by a runtime; (2) DIRECTIONAL MAPPING CONTRACT: runtimes declare mappings FROM local roles TO neutral roles via DomainDefinition.roleMappings (Scholar: principal→ADMINISTRATOR, teacher→CONTRIBUTOR, bursar→OPERATOR, driver→WORKER, student/parent→MEMBER; restaurant fixture: manager→ADMINISTRATOR/OWNER, cashier→OPERATOR, service_staff→WORKER, runner→WORKER) — the platform never learns a domain role name, never the reverse mapping; (3) CAPABILITY-BASED AUTHORIZATION: capability codes evaluate against neutral roles/grants resolved from cg_role_assignment/cg_role_grant, with runtime-declared feature declarations replacing MEMBERSHIP_FOR_NAV_KIND and the hard-coded 'r001'; (4) NEUTRAL TENANT MEMBERSHIP PRIMITIVES: get_my_tenant_id() + holds_tenant_role() over universal membership tables as the gate for every universal cg_ substrate RPC and the RLS activation dependency for cg_org_unit/cg_org_membership (I-007); (5) RUNTIME-DECLARED WORKSPACE KINDS: nav/workspace kinds contributed per runtime, not a fixed Scholar enum; (6) NEUTRAL IDENTITY ACTOR: IdentityActor carries tenantRef + neutral roles; domain adapters translate identity-store rows at the boundary. Deny-by-default is authoritative: any authorization state not explicitly granted is DENY; REDACT/ESCALATE/REQUIRE_APPROVAL are the only non-binary refinements and each resolves through an owned governed flow.
authorization.denyByDefaultCompliance: STRONG IN DESIGN, PARTIALLY PROVEN. Compliant: zero-policy RLS on every authored cg_ table (deny unless policy); files access-policy denies every non-allow path including super-admin cross-tenant; ai-gateway fails closed on missing key and refuses unconfigured invocation; workflow engine never resolves UNKNOWN to TRUE; notification state machine cannot reach 'delivered' without provider receipt; foundation-loop refuses caller-supplied tenant/verification. Not yet proven: RLS posture is statically reasoned (J-041, L-H-008); authorization.ts — the engine itself — has no dedicated exhaustive suite (STREAM H: highest-stakes module, least directly tested, L-H-022); ESCALATE/REQUIRE_APPROVAL outcomes lack wired resolution flows (J-032, L-H-016); identity revocation/expiry fail-closed is unproven (J-009).

dataLifecycle.retention: V1CAP-066 (privacy & retention lifecycle, owner phase 03 with 14 and 09) is a named capability with no implementation. AI snapshot retention is boundary-declared ('snapshots redacted per AI privacy pipeline; retention aligned to V1CAP-066') but the policy itself does not exist. Evidence records (cg_foundation_evidence) carry no retention policy (J-033 lifecycle: sufficiency, confidence, revocation, staleness, retention — all absent).
dataLifecycle.erasureVsImmutableAudit: THE CENTRAL TENSION, EXPLICITLY UNRESOLVED: AGENTS 28 mandates immutable audit records while personal-data erasure (Constitution §19 privacy law) demands forgetting. J-039 captures the required reconciliation — what may be forgotten, what may not, and how both are recorded — as a major gap with no owner-authored design. Current posture: all cg_ substrate tables are append-leaning (cg_event append-only by design, V1CAP-041), so erasure semantics for personal data inside immutable streams is undesigned. Recommendation recorded as L-H-019-adjacent design duty under V1CAP-066; crypto-shredding or tenant-scoped redaction layers are the candidate mechanisms and must be decided in the V1CAP-066 contract, not improvised.
dataLifecycle.backup: V1CAP-074/J-042: none. Backup/restore and verified recovery for tenant data and evidence stores is a named capability (impl=false); no backup exists for the dev project where the two approved migrations were applied; rollback SQL exists for 20260929000000/20260930000000/20261001000000 (authoring-time artifacts, not backups).
dataLifecycle.verdict: GAP. Retention, erasure-vs-immutable-audit reconciliation, and backup/recovery are all unimplemented V1 capabilities with named owners. The evidence-critical path (V1CAP-002→042→044→059) hardens capture and provenance but not lifecycle. Data lifecycle must close before personal data at production scale enters the substrate (privacy law precedence in the governance hierarchy); it does not gate first loop closure on non-personal operational data. Tracked as L-H-026.

migration.riskAnalysis: Three ordered risks. (1) TYPE-DIVERGENCE: tenant_id is text in 20261001000000 (org model) and uuid-flavored in legacy Scholar tables; the divergence is explicitly deferred to the operator (COND-003). Resolving it AFTER the neutral helper ships would force a breaking re-gate of every universal RPC; it must be ruled BEFORE L-H-001's migration is authored. (2) IDENTITY SPLIT: promoting cg_identity over public.users (I-001) touches the live identity store of the running Scholar app — requires ADR, dual-write period, evidence preservation, and a rollback plan (CHANGE MANAGEMENT §38); destructive steps are forbidden (NO DESTRUCTIVE REFACTORING §39). verification.independenceOfVerification: J-035 captures the twin gap: (a) the evidence lifecycle lacks sufficiency assessment, confidence, revocation, staleness detection and retention (J-033), and (b) verification independence — a worker (AI or human) cannot verify its own output — is required by the corpus (E-050, ENFORCED class) but enforced nowhere outside the foundation loop's structural admission/verification separation. The foundation loop is the only place independence holds today, and it holds by engine design (foundation-loop.ts refuses caller-supplied verification decisions), not by a generalizable independence rule over identities.
